_doc: Every gate of experiment/playbook-uplift/verification-playbook.txt (sections 3.1-3.8, 5, 5a-5c), with the IVG counterpart where the playbook's example is PostgreSQL- or ERP-specific. scope: 'product' (one cell for the whole product), 'module' (one cell per module 00-18), or 'module-writer' (modules that write stored state). applies_unless: a source-cited reason a module is genuinely not applicable. build_matrix.py combines this catalog with the inventories and the lanes' evidence.

gates.text: every statement's parent id resolves; tree from the module root
Flesch-Kincaid grade <= 8 on statement text
every module-glossary term a statement uses is defined by an ancestor or an earlier same-parent statement (literal rule)
INDEX.md regenerates without manual edits
every (entity state x command) cell defined or assigned to a human decision
statements cover the module's actual public entry points, storage owners, background jobs, native paths and lifecycle operations (reconciled against a source inventory)
each open decision has independently recovered intent with sources, contradictions, as-built vs intended, working assumption and alternatives
environment modelled as a reusable library (IVG: IRIS 2026.1 contract instead of pgspec)
differential validation against the real engine with 0 outcomes outside the permitted set
sharpness tests (the model forbids plausible-but-wrong outcomes; permitted sets small)
every environment-model mutant detected
every IRIS feature the module relies on is inside the contract's semantic subset or explicitly marked outside it
a small L1 model with the module's business invariants
an L2 machine over the real data layout
every L2 operation refines an L1 step or a permitted stutter (proved)
broken-implementation controls each rejected by a proof
cross-module behaviours as Protocol2 over participant contracts, with progress under named fairness
progress controls fail only the progress proof
proof cost measured per crate
bounded model check of the module's operations with negative controls and sharpness (explorer); as-built vs reviewed where a finding exists
universal axioms stated
shared mechanisms with state, operations, events, L1 laws, generic lemmas proved once over a trait, and generic controls (playbook §3.3a item 2)
canonical lifecycles; every object declares lifecycle, mechanisms, axioms
domain contract for the central component (ERP: ledger fold) -> IVG: replay of the revision ledger equals the governed store
gates.counterpart: ERP ledger -> IVG revision ledger replay (RPL)

gates.text: every (invariant, writer plan) pair has a preservation lemma, guard or recorded finding; writer inventory derived from source, not hand-declared only
every requirement traces to an axiom, contract clause or named exception
every storage statement proved equal to the model's evaluation (IVG: IRIS SQL statements and ObjectScript global operations against the IRIS contract)
gates.counterpart: pgspec statement lemmas -> IRIS statement/global correspondence

gates.text: ownership check (single write owner per table/global) with a self-test
no reliance on storage or insertion order, with a self-test
each query reads only its declared footprint, with a self-test
generated statement code changes only through its generator
gates.na_reason: IVG has no generated statement code: SQL and ObjectScript are hand-written (iris_src/src, iris_vector_graph); the parity gate has no object. Not applicable at the pin.

gates.text: every handler proved to perform its spec step under an abstraction (IVG: Python/ObjectScript entry points)
lock-plan obligations proved per handler (IVG: LOCK names, SQL row locks, head lock)
decoders and status maps verified (IVG: JSON/$LIST result decoders, error-code -> exception maps, HTTP status maps)
zero default lint warnings (Rust clippy) -> IVG counterpart: the product's own configured linters
style review passes
a committed transaction refines the serial step; chained over whole executions
frame obligation per statement-shape class
well-formedness under row permutation
row-id and key invariants
foreign keys
capacity (IRIS: string/subscript length, lock-table and lock-escalation thresholds, max batch sizes)
condition list (SQL_CLOSURE.md counterpart) exact; every premise maps to a test
the explorers run
crash, lost acknowledgement, disconnect worlds
the differential suite
end-to-end tests on 1 and N application processes/nodes (multi-process and multi-node distinguished)
trace replay of real runs through the machines
database statement/lock log checked against the lock plan
mutation testing of the unverified layers
A/B performance of existing baseline configurations incl. spec 256 SC-002/SC-003
failure scenarios each with a negative control
existing suites (unit, integration, e2e, contract, TCK, docs) rerun on the unchanged pin with triage
supported editions/versions compared (Community 2026.1 here; Enterprise/2026.3 if available)
a full rerun from clean builds, each result recorded
STATUS.md with each guarantee's level, status and conditions
trust inventory
test reflection
independent reviewer signs off spec against intent
every finding becomes a fix or a recorded decision (observation-only: a recorded finding with evidence and disposition; the product obligation stays failed/open)
exact trusted-item list; strict gate pins expected failures
mutants for every layer, each kill located in the expected file; inconclusive reruns
self-tests for every structural check
one heavy job at a time, time caps, disk floor, wait timeouts, stop by PID
every unproved obligation listed in a proof-debt file; nothing reported proved without a decisive run
one gate = one build on one machine within 20 minutes (the fast entry point)
claims measured through the client's entry point (IVG: DB-API/Native API path the product uses)
where the outcome depends on something unfixed, the model admits every outcome or refuses
stated refusals (X statements) audited mechanically: each implemented and evidenced, or recorded
findings grouped by root cause
independent reviewers early with different angles incl. a randomized simulator through the real engine checking global invariants after every commit
